cards.text: The famine is still severe in the land, and Jacob's family has eaten all the grain they brought back from Egypt. So Jacob tells his sons, "Go back and buy us a little more food." A LITTLE more, friend, which is exactly what I say every time I open the chocolate chips.
But Judah, one of Jacob's sons, pushes back. He reminds his dad what the man in Egypt solemnly warned them, and friend, "solemnly" is never followed by good news.

cards.question: According to Judah, what did the man in Egypt warn the brothers?

answers.text: They won't see his face again without their brother
They won't get more grain unless they pay double
They won't leave Egypt alive a second time

cards.question: Judah tells his father the brothers will go down to Egypt either way, whether their brother comes or not.

cards.text: Their father Jacob, also called Israel, asks them, "Why did you bring this trouble upon me?" Friend, that's the voice of a dad staring into an EMPTY cookie jar.

cards.question: Israel has one more question for his sons. What does he blame them for?

answers.text: Telling the man they had another brother
Coming home with too little grain
Bowing down to the man in Egypt

cards.text: The brothers say the man questioned them in detail: "Is your father still alive? Do you have another brother?" They just answered, so how could they possibly know he'd say bring your brother here?
Then Judah speaks up again. He tells his father to send the boy, Benjamin, with him so they can go at once and live and not die, Jacob and their children included.

cards.question: Judah makes his father an offer about Benjamin. What is it?

answers.text: He'll give his own two sons as a pledge
He'll hire guards to watch over Benjamin

cards.question: Judah also points out that if they hadn't delayed, they could have gone to Egypt and come back twice by now.

cards.text: Israel finally gives in. If it must be so, he says, then here's what they'll do: pack the best products of the land as a gift for the man. That's the oldest move there is, friend: when in doubt, bring a cookie box.

cards.question: What goes into Israel's gift for the man in Egypt?

answers.text: Wine and figs and olive oil

cards.question: Israel also tells them to take ___ the silver, so they can return the silver that was put back in their sacks.

cards.text: Israel says perhaps the silver was a mistake. Then come the words I bet he's been dreading: "Take your brother as well, and return to the man at once."

cards.question: Israel tells his sons, "May God Almighty grant you mercy before the man, that he may release your other brother along with Benjamin."
Then Israel says, "As for me, if I am bereaved, I am bereaved." What does he mean?

answers.text: He's ready to accept losing his sons
He's sure the man will send them back
He's planning to go down to Egypt himself

cards.text: So the men take the gifts, double the silver and Benjamin, and they hurry down to Egypt and stand before Joseph. Round two, friend. And this time Benjamin is in the room.
In Egypt, Joseph sees Benjamin standing there with his brothers. Then he turns to the steward who runs his house and gives an order.

cards.question: What does Joseph tell his steward to do with the brothers?

answers.text: Take them home and prepare a meal
Lock them up for three days
Send them straight back to Canaan

cards.text: The steward takes them to Joseph's house, and the brothers are frightened. It's that "hey, can you come by my office" feeling, except the boss runs EGYPT.

cards.question: Because of the silver returned in their bags, the brothers are afraid the Egyptians will overpower them and take them as slaves, donkeys and all.

cards.text: So they catch the steward at the entrance and explain everything: they found their silver in their sacks, they brought it all back plus more to buy food, and they don't know who put it there. Friend, I talk exactly like that every time a cookie goes missing and I'm the only one in the bakery.

cards.question: The steward tells the brothers it's fine and not to be afraid. Who does he say gave them the treasure in their sacks?

answers.text: Their God the God of their father
A servant who made a mistake

cards.question: Then the steward brings someone out to the brothers. Who is it?

cards.text: The steward takes them inside, gives them water to wash their feet and feeds their donkeys. They went from bracing to be taken as slaves to a foot-washing in six verses, and now they're getting their gift ready for Joseph at noon.
When Joseph comes home, they present him with the gifts and bow to the ground before him.

cards.question: Joseph asks if they're well. Then he asks how their elderly ___ is, the one they told him about.
The brothers tell Joseph that their father has died.

cards.text: Then Joseph looks up and sees Benjamin, his own mother's son. He asks, "Is this your youngest brother, the one you told me about?" and then he says, "May God be gracious to you, my son."

cards.question: Right after blessing Benjamin, Joseph hurries out. Why?

answers.text: He's moved to tears for his brother
He's angry the brothers lied to him
He's been called away by Pharaoh

cards.text: He goes to a private room and weeps. Then he washes his face, pulls himself together, comes back out and says, "Serve the meal."

cards.question: The meal is served separately to Joseph, the brothers and the Egyptians. Why don't the Egyptians eat with the brothers?

answers.text: Eating with Hebrews was detestable to them
The brothers were still under arrest
There wasn't room for everyone together

cards.text: Then the brothers are seated before Joseph in order by age, from the firstborn down to the youngest. Eleven brothers in one neat row.

cards.question: Seated in order by age, the brothers look at one another in astonishment.
The portions are served from Joseph's table, and Benjamin's portion is ___ times larger than any of the others.

cards.text: So they feast and drink freely with Joseph. I'm setting this batch on the rack for now, friend, but this story is NOT done baking.

findings.problem: Genesis 43 picks up in the middle of the Joseph story, but the opening card gives none of the earlier events that this passage depends on. It never says that the brothers already went to Egypt, that 'the man' kept one brother (Simeon) there, or that their silver turned up in their sacks. Later cards lean on all three: card 2's 'the man in Egypt,' card 13's 'silver that was put back in their sacks' and card 15's 'release your other brother.' The same gap affects stop 2 card 7, where 'Their brother Simeon' appears with no explanation of why he is in Egypt.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on. If the passage starts in the middle of a thought, it gives the context.

findings.problem: Benjamin is named here for the first time as just 'the boy, Benjamin.' The card never says who he is, such as Jacob's youngest son. Judah, by contrast, was introduced as 'one of Jacob's sons.'

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: Joseph shows up here as 'stand before Joseph' with no word on who he is. Nothing tells the baker that Joseph is 'the man' the brothers keep talking about, or that he is their brother. Without that, Joseph's tears in stop 2 (Genesis 43:30) and the seating by age (Genesis 43:33) are hard to follow.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The joke 'that's the voice of a dad staring into an EMPTY cookie jar' is a parent scolding kids over a cookie jar, which is a scenario aimed at kids. The empty jar also blends with the Bible setting, since the family's grain really has run out. The actual core action of Genesis 43:6 is blaming the sons for telling the man about Benjamin.

rule.text: No jokes or scenarios about school, parents or anything aimed at kids. Work, bosses and bills are fine.

findings.problem: The joke 'every time a cookie goes missing and I'm the only one in the bakery' only works if the speaker is guilty, which makes the brothers' explanation sound like a guilty cover-up. In Genesis 43:20-22 they are honestly reporting silver that showed up in their sacks. They did not take anything, so the comparison does not match the action.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The right answer 'Take them home and prepare a meal' is unclear about whose home is meant. 'Home' could be read as the brothers' home, which overlaps with the wrong answer 'Send them straight back to Canaan.' Genesis 43:16 says Joseph's house.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.
